additions.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Predicting Tar and Gas Distributions During Coal Pyrolysis and Exploring Structure–Product Relationships
additions.abstract: A framework coupling reactive molecular dynamics (ReaxFF MD) with interpretable machine learning was developed to relate coal molecular structure to pyrolysis product distributions. Pyrolysis simulations of 161 coal macromolecular models spanning different ranks were conducted under consistent conditions. Feature selection, model comparison, and cross-validation yielded separate models for semicoke, light tar, heavy tar, pyrolysis gas, and pyrolysis water mass fractions. Within this simulation dataset, gradient boosting regression (GBR), partial least squares regression (PLS), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) performed best for semicoke, pyrolysis gas, and heavy tar, respectively, with test-set R2 values of 0.9920, 0.9977, and 0.8909. The light tar XGBoost and pyrolysis water random forest (RF) models achieved test-set R2 values of 0.6295 and 0.6214. Their relatively limited predictive ability may reflect limited sample size and difficulty capturing secondary reactions and dynamic structural evolution using initial static descriptors. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis ranked O-linked methylene and the H/C ratio highest by mean |SHAP| in the heavy tar and pyrolysis gas models, respectively. Accumulated local effects (ALE) and individual conditional expectation (ICE) analyses indicated generally positive associations between counts of O-linked methylene and ether bridges and predicted heavy tar mass fractions. Heavy tar model responses to the O/C and H/C ratios varied across ranges and samples. Pyrolysis gas predictions generally responded positively to the H/C ratio, degree of aromatic substitution, and Num naphthenic rings. This framework predicts product distributions and interprets structure–product relationships within a specified ReaxFF MD system, informing coal structure screening and targeted product control.
